{{Short description|Hungarian mathematician}}
[[File:Beke Manó.JPEG|thumb|{{center|Manó Beke}}]]
'''Emanuel Beke''' (Beke Manó {{in lang|hu}}, 24 April 1862, [[Pápa]] – 27 June 1946, Budapest) was a Hungarian mathematician, specializing in differential equations,<ref>Beke, Emanuel. "Die Irreducibilität der homogenen linearen Differentialgleichungen." Mathematische Annalen 45, no. 2 (1894): 278–294. {{doi|10.1007/BF01446541}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=On integrability by quadratures|author=Epsteen, Saul|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|volume=9|year=1902|issue=3 |pages=152–154|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1902-00966-X|doi-access=free|url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/bulletin-of-the-american-mathematical-society/volume-9/issue-3/On-integrability-by-quadratures/bams/1183417273.pdf}} Epsteen shows that what he calls the "Jordan–Beke theorem" implies the "Vessiot theorem" in [[Picard–Vessiot theory]].</ref> determinants, and mathematical physics. He is known for reforming the teaching of mathematics in Hungary.<ref name=Horvath>{{cite book|editor=Horváth, János|chapter=Beke Manó|year=2006|title=A Panorama of Hungarian Mathematics in the Twentieth Century, I|pages=567–568|publisher=Springer in collaboration with János Bolyai Mathematical Society|isbn=9783540307211 |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EWm4WzSaG3IC&pg=PA567}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|editor=Beke, E.|editor2=Mikola, S.|title=Abhandlungen über die Reform des mathematischen Unterrichts in Ungarn|location=Leipzig|publisher=Teubner|year=1911|postscript=; vi+166 pp.|url=https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/012310013}}</ref>

==Education and career==
At the [[University of Budapest]] he received a mathematics-physics degree in 1883 and a doctorate in 1884.<ref>{{cite web|title=Beke Manó|url=http://mek.oszk.hu/00300/00355/html/ABC00523/01385.htm|website=mek.oszk.hu}} brief bio {{in lang|hu}}</ref>

{{blockquote|He taught at a secondary school in Budapest until 1895, and spent the year 1892/93 in Göttingen with a scholarship. He became aware of the activities of [[Felix Klein]] concerning the reform of the teaching of mathematics, and after his return he became the leader of the reformers of teaching of mathematics in Hungary. In 1895 he started teaching at the Mintagimnázium in Budapest. In 1900 he was appointed professor at the University of Budapest.<ref name=Horvath/>}}

In 1908 he was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in Rome.<ref>{{cite book|author=Beke, E.|chapter=Ueber den jetzigen Stand des mathematischen Unterrichtes und die Reformbestrebungen in Ungarn|pages=530–533|volume=3|title=Atti del IV Congresso internazionale dei matematici (Roma, 6–11 Aprile 1908)|series=ICM proceedings |year=1897 |publisher=University of Toronto Press |chapter-url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=iau.31858027749682;view=1up;seq=554}}</ref> In 1914 he was elected a corresponding member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]]. In 1922 the official Council of the University of Budapest condemned his political activity, dismissed him from the University, and took away his membership in the Hungarian Academy of Sciences. After his dismissal he worked for a publishing firm.<ref name=Horvath/>

Since 1950 the [[János Bolyai Mathematical Society]] has awarded the Máno Beke Commemorative Prize for teaching and popularization of mathematics.
